documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Visit date: 01/04/2023

Mr. Fleming is a 76-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, prior stroke and multi-infarct dementia, accompanied by his daughter, referred for urinary symptoms and an elevated PSA. He has to strain to begin voiding, the stream is intermittent, and he gets up several times a night. He notes a dull lower abdominal discomfort. No flank pain, gross hematuria or fevers. Appetite is preserved but he has lost weight over the last few months without trying.

PMH: as above, plus aortic stenosis and presbycusis. No previous urologic procedures or surgery.
Meds: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, metformin 500 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20 mg, loratadine as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: older brother with prostate cancer.
Social: never smoker.

Exam: abdomen soft, no masses, bladder not palpable. DRE: prostate hard and irregular with nodularity.

Data: PSA 48.6 (11/2022, primary care), markedly elevated.

Assessment: findings highly suspicious for prostate cancer.

Plan: multiparametric prostate MRI, then transrectal biopsy. Discussed with patient and daughter, who agree. Will see them after biopsy.

Urology

documents.title: Urology letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Urology consult received. Suspicious exam; MRI and biopsy being arranged.

documents.title: MRI prostate with and without contrast
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
MRI PROSTATE, MULTIPARAMETRIC (performed 01/19/2023)
Indication: PSA 48.6, abnormal DRE.

Findings: enlarged prostate. A large lesion in the peripheral zone with marked restricted diffusion and early enhancement. Tumor extends through the prostatic capsule and into the adjacent seminal vesicles. Bladder wall and rectum are preserved. No enlarged pelvic lymph nodes. No suspicious marrow lesions in the imaged pelvis.

Impression: findings of prostate cancer with extracapsular extension into the seminal vesicles.

reports.text:
Specimen: prostate, transrectal ultrasound-guided needle biopsies, 12 cores (sextant bilateral, medial and lateral).
Microscopic: prostatic adenocarcinoma, acinar type, present in 8 of 12 cores. Gleason score 4+4=8 (Grade Group 4).
reports.conclusion: Prostatic adenocarcinoma, Gleason 4+4=8 (Grade Group 4), 8 of 12 cores.

documents.title: Prostate biopsy
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
PROCEDURE: transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy, 12 cores, 01/24/2023, under local block with prophylactic antibiotic. Daughter present for consent; patient assented and understood the procedure. Tolerated well, no immediate complications. Discharged home.

Pathology: adenocarcinoma, Gleason 4+4=8, Grade Group 4, 8 of 12 cores. Staging CT abdomen/pelvis and bone scan ordered; return visit to discuss treatment.

Urology

documents.title: Biopsy results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: MRI and pathology reports in today. Called daughter; urology had already told them it is cancer. Reviewed in plain terms: high-grade prostate cancer that has grown just outside the gland; staging scans next; treatment is usually hormone therapy with or without radiation and urology will go through it. She asked whether his dementia changes anything; told her it is part of choosing the gentlest effective plan and that we will support whatever they decide. Problem list updated.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys normal. No hydronephrosis. No enlarged retroperitoneal or pelvic lymph nodes. Prostate enlarged. Bladder normally distended. No ascites. No lytic or blastic bone lesions. Mild degenerative change of the lumbar spine.
reports.conclusion: No lymphadenopathy or osseous metastatic disease.

documents.title: Bone scan
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
WHOLE-BODY BONE SCAN (02/07/2023)
Indication: newly diagnosed prostate adenocarcinoma.
Findings: physiologic tracer distribution. Mild uptake at the lower cervical spine and knees consistent with degenerative change. No pattern of metastatic disease.
Impression: no scintigraphic evidence of osseous metastases.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth daily for 4 weeks
22.5 mg intramuscularly every 3 months, given in urology office; first dose 2/28/2023

documents.title: Urology follow-up: treatment plan
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
UROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 02/14/2023

Seen with daughter (health care proxy) to review results.
Pathology: adenocarcinoma, Gleason 4+4=8 (Grade Group 4), 8/12 cores. MRI: extracapsular extension into seminal vesicles. CT abdomen/pelvis: no adenopathy, no bone lesions. Bone scan negative.

Assessment: locally advanced, nonmetastatic high-risk prostate cancer.

Discussion: options of androgen deprivation with radiation versus androgen deprivation alone. Given his age, vascular dementia and wish to avoid daily treatment trips, patient and daughter prefer androgen deprivation alone with close PSA follow-up. Side effects reviewed: hot flashes, fatigue, weight and muscle change, glucose effects, bone thinning.

Plan:
- Bicalutamide 50 mg daily for 4 weeks, starting today.
- Leuprolide 22.5 mg IM every 3 months, first injection 2/28.
- PSA in 3 months.

Urology

documents.title: Urology letter (late)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Letter from the 2/14 urology visit finally received. ADT alone: bicalutamide x4 weeks (finished), leuprolide q3 months. Medication list updated.

documents.title: Hormone shot
documents.author: patient
documents.body: This is George's daughter. He got his first hormone shot at urology last week and is taking a pill from them for a month. They decided against radiation. Do you have their notes? He has been a bit warm at night but otherwise ok.

documents.title: RE: Hormone shot
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for the update. We have not received the urology note yet and have asked for it. Night sweats and warmth are common with this treatment. We will update his medication list once the note arrives; keep a list of what he is taking handy. See you both in April.

documents.title: Records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Requested urology note from 2/14/23 and treatment plan.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up, new prostate cancer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Second leuprolide due late May. Hot flashes at night, sleeping with a fan. Urinating somewhat easier, still up twice at night. Weight steady since winter. Memory unchanged. No falls.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Mild left weakness, gait steady. Basal systolic murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet intact.

A/P:
1. Prostate adenocarcinoma, locally advanced, on androgen deprivation via urology. Reviewed the plan with them.
2. T2DM: yearly labs; ADT can raise sugars a little.
3. HTN, HLD, aortic stenosis, dementia: unchanged.
RTC May for wellness visit.

documents.title: Yearly labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c slightly higher than last year, still acceptable for him. Kidney and liver tests, counts and lipids fine. No change.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
WELLNESS VISIT with daughter.

ADLs independent; IADLs by daughter. Not driving. Uses microwave, stove disabled. No falls. Hearing aids daily.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 1/3; daughter sees no big change this year.
PHQ-9 5, more tired since hormone shots.
Advance directive and proxy on file; MOLST reviewed and deferred again at his request.
Vaccines: due for RSV this fall; COVID and flu in fall. Tdap due next year.

Exam: mild left weakness, systolic murmur, lungs clear.

Plan: diabetes check July.

documents.title: Urology follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

Mr. Fleming returned for his 3-month review on androgen deprivation. PSA has fallen from 48.6 to 6.2. Voiding is improved. Hot flashes tolerable. Second leuprolide 22.5 mg given today. Next PSA and injection in about 6 months with an injection visit between.

Urology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daughter with him. PSA dropping per urology. Hot flashes less. Allergies ok. Walks the block with her in the evenings. Exam unchanged from spring. A1c and BMP. Continue.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No change. Proxy note to daughter.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Dilated exam for diabetes: no retinopathy in either eye. Cataracts unchanged; patient and daughter decline surgical referral at present. Return 1 year.

Optometry

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu high-dose IM right deltoid; 2023-24 COVID vaccine IM left deltoid. Daughter will take him to the pharmacy for RSV later this month (not yet stocked here).

documents.title: Pharmacy immunization record
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Notification from his community pharmacy via the state registry: RSV vaccine (adjuvanted) given 10/24/2023. Entered in immunization history.

documents.title: Urology follow-up
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Mr. Fleming continues leuprolide every 3 months. PSA today 1.4, down from 6.2 in May. Mild nocturia, stream acceptable. Injection given. Return in 6 months with PSA.

Urology

events.reason: Unable to urinate, lower abdominal pain

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE
Date of service: 01/03/2024

CC: cannot pass urine.

HPI: 77-year-old man brought by his daughter. Lower abdominal pain and no urine output for the last 24 hours. Followed by urology for suspected prostate cancer; a year of gradually weaker stream and nighttime voiding. Two days ago he began a nonprescription allergy tablet that he had heard might help his symptoms; daughter did not bring the box.

PMH: hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide, seasonal allergic rhinitis, diabetes, dementia, prior stroke, aortic stenosis.
Meds (per daughter): metformin 500 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, loratadine 10 mg as needed, hydrochlorothiazide, the OTC allergy product.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 145/90, HR 78. Uncomfortable. Lower abdomen distended with a palpable, tender bladder. DRE: prostate enlarged, smooth and firm. Mucous membranes dry. No new focal neurological deficit.

Labs: creatinine 1.2, BUN 19, potassium 4.5, sodium 140.

Course: urethral catheter placed with prompt relief and a large volume drained. Comfortable afterward.

Impression: acute urinary retention, likely the OTC allergy medication on top of prostatic obstruction.

Disposition: home with indwelling catheter and leg bag. Stop the OTC allergy product. Urology for voiding trial within a week. Return for fever, catheter blockage or bleeding.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: ED record (late)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 1/3 finally received. Matches what the daughter reported. Retention added to problem list.

documents.title: Daughter: ED last night
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter called. Took him to the ED last night, he could not pee all day and was in pain. They put in a catheter and sent him home; urology Tuesday to take it out. He had started some allergy-sinus pills from the drugstore 2 days ago; she does not know which ones and has thrown them out. Catheter draining clear yellow, no fever. Reviewed catheter care and reasons to call. Told her no OTC cold or allergy products without asking us; loratadine alone is fine. Asked her to have ED send records.

documents.title: Voiding trial
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Daughter: catheter removed at urology yesterday and he passed the voiding trial, urinating on his own since. Stream weak but steady. Keeping 1/16 follow-up here.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. ED 1/3 for urinary retention after an OTC allergy-sinus product; catheter, then voiding trial passed 1/9 at urology. Voiding since, weak stream, up twice at night. No fever, no burning. Only loratadine for allergies now.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Abdomen soft, bladder not palpable. Mild left weakness. Systolic murmur. Lungs clear.

A/P:
1. Urinary retention, resolved after catheter; precipitant stopped. UA today. Medication list reviewed with daughter: avoid antihistamine-decongestant combinations and sleep aids.
2. Yearly labs. ED creatinine 1.2 when dry; recheck today.
3. Prostate cancer on ADT; next urology in May.
We still do not have the ED record.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine back to his usual. A1c, lipids, counts fine. UA clean. Portal note to daughter.

medications.drug: amoxicillin 875 MG / clavulanate 125 MG Oral Tablet
medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days

documents.title: Pharmacy notice
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy called to ask whether to add a new antibiotic to his blister pack: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg twice daily x 7 days, filled 3/9 from an urgent care prescriber. We had no notice of the visit. Told them to dispense as written, separate card. Will call daughter.

documents.title: Urgent care visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Reached daughter. Saturday she took him to an urgent care for cough and fever; they told her it was pneumonia and gave the antibiotic. She does not have paperwork. Today: cough looser, no fever since Sunday, eating and drinking. No shortness of breath at rest. Advised to finish the course. Follow-up visit booked April. Asked her to request the urgent care note.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Treated for pneumonia at an urgent care in March (no record received). Finished antibiotics, cough gone, energy back. No fever.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, saturation normal. Lungs clear to auscultation throughout. Systolic murmur. Mild left weakness.

A/P: pneumonia resolved clinically. A1c today. Wellness visit next month with Tdap.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
WELLNESS VISIT with daughter.

Year: urinary retention in January, pneumonia in March, both recovered. ADT continuing.
Function: self-care independent; daughter handles the rest, daily visits. No falls.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 1/3; gradual change per daughter.
PHQ-9 4.
Hearing aids, glasses. Abstinent from alcohol.
Tdap given today (last 2014).
Advance directive current.

Exam: mild left weakness; systolic murmur; lungs clear.

Plan: follow-up July.

documents.title: Urology update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Daughter here. Urology last week said his PSA is 0.8, the lowest yet, and gave his shot. They said all is going as hoped. I don't think they send you letters every time.

documents.title: RE: Urology update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good news, thank you. I've noted it in his chart.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Daughter: eating more slowly lately and sometimes coughs at the table; she cuts his food smaller. He has no complaints. Weight about the same. Exam: lungs clear, systolic murmur, mild left weakness. Labs today. Will keep an eye on weight and swallowing.

documents.title: Labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: BMP and A1c fine. Portal to daughter.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Annual diabetic eye check for George Fleming: retinas clear of diabetic retinopathy both sides. Cataracts stable. Return 12 months.

Optometry

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Patchy airspace opacity in the right lower lobe. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Same-day visit: cough, fever
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Daughter texted this morning; seen same day.

HPI: three days of wet cough and fever at home, more tired, eating less. Second chest infection this year (March, urgent care). Daughter again mentions coughing during meals and some bringing up of food at night.

EXAM: vitals per flowsheet. Not in distress, speaking full sentences. Crackles at the right base. Basal systolic murmur. Mild left weakness.

CXR in office: right lower lobe opacity. WBC 13.2.

A/P: right lower lobe pneumonia, outpatient treatment reasonable (alert, oral intake ok, saturation normal, daughter with him daily). Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg twice daily for 7 days. Fluids. Return precautions: breathing harder, confusion, unable to take pills. Recheck in 2 weeks; we will look at the swallowing then.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
With daughter. Finished antibiotic; cough gone, no fever.

Swallowing: since early summer solids seem to stick, comes and goes. At night he sometimes brings up food that looks undigested. Bad breath despite brushing. Says there is a lump feeling in his throat. Liquids mostly fine.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet, weight down a couple of kg. Lungs clear now. Neck without obvious mass on my exam today. Mild left weakness. Systolic murmur.

A/P:
1. Pneumonia resolved.
2. Intermittent solid dysphagia with regurgitation and two pneumonias this year: GI referral.
3. Weight loss, likely from eating less; soft, moist foods and small bites meanwhile.
4. Flu and COVID vaccines today.
